original_question: Let X be a compact topological space, and let H be a subgroup of S(X), the semigroup of continuous self-maps of X. Suppose H acts transitively on X and is distal, meaning that for any distinct points x1 and x2 in X and any point x in X there exists a neighborhood U of x such that {h(x1), h(x2)} is not contained in U for all h in H. Must H be left bounded?
target_in_paper: Problem 5 (Protasov): Let X be a compact space and H be a distal subgroup of S(X), acting transitively on X. Is H left bounded?
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right target: it keeps the ambient compact space X, the semigroup S(X) of continuous self-maps, the transitivity assumption, the paper's distal condition, and the exact converse-type question about left boundedness. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=a5aa9d40ecf3b293a0f89c8e540d8733a329d406&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper explicitly fixes the topology on S(X): it is the topology of pointwise convergence inherited from the Tychonoff product X^X. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=a5aa9d40ecf3b293a0f89c8e540d8733a329d406&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

Because left boundedness is a topological notion, H should be understood with the subspace topology inherited from S(X). ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=a5aa9d40ecf3b293a0f89c8e540d8733a329d406&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The paper defines “left bounded” for a semigroup S with identity e as: for every neighborhood U of e there exists a finite set F⊂S such that S = FU. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=a5aa9d40ecf3b293a0f89c8e540d8733a329d406&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The paper states the problem as an open problem due to Protasov and does not add extra separation, metrizability, or algebraic hypotheses beyond compactness of X, transitivity, and distality. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=a5aa9d40ecf3b293a0f89c8e540d8733a329d406&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let X be a compact space, and let S(X)⊂X^X be the semigroup of all continuous self-maps of X, endowed with the topology of pointwise convergence inherited from the Tychonoff product X^X. Suppose H is a subgroup of S(X) that acts transitively on X and is distal, in the sense that for any distinct points x1,x2∈X and any point x∈X there exists a neighborhood U of x such that {h(x1),h(x2)}⊄U for every h∈H. Must H be left bounded; equivalently, for every neighborhood V of the identity e in H, is there a finite set F⊂H such that H = FV?
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper. The paper first defines left/right bounded semigroups and fixes S(X) as the semigroup of continuous self-maps of X with the pointwise-convergence topology; it then defines distal subgroups H⊂S(X) and records that [11, Theorem 4] proves one direction: a left bounded subgroup acting transitively on X is distal. Problem 5 asks whether the converse holds when X is compact. Your draft is therefore very close, but to be fully stand-alone and paper-faithful it must make the ambient topology and the definition of left bounded explicit. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=a5aa9d40ecf3b293a0f89c8e540d8733a329d406&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
